newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Showpla Asia to diversify across markets.
newsitem.headline: Showpla Asia to diversify across markets.

text.p: Showpla Asia Ltd (SAL) plans to move into emerging economies and diversify product outlets to sustain growth in the next few years, company chief Kenzo Nakagawa said on Wednesday.
"I'm optimistic growth will be sustained. We will have higher contributions from China, Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia," Nakagawa told a news conference.
He said the company was also seeing growth from emerging Brazilian and Indian markets.
The company had been able to avoid a drop in profitability during the recent electronics slump in part by profits in these countries, he said.
SAL, a manufacturer of injection-moulded plastic components for the consumer electronic and telecommunications industries, will also diversify into automobiles and computers, he said.
Company officials did not say when SAL would begin producing parts for automobiles and computers, but said it should make inroads into the auto industry soon.
"There is more competition in computer peripherals right now. The situation is better in the auto industry," said Teruyuki Nakagawa, senior executive vice president of Showa Plastics Co.
He said SAL would strive to extend the successful application of its new technologies -- tooling die fabrication and blow moulding -- in the emerging markets.
"We will look at opportunities to expand into higher value-added and fast growing industries to broaden our customer base," he said.
SAL's net profit for 1996 rose 7.1 percent to Singapore $4.17 million on a turnover of $129.87 million.
The rise in turnover was due to increased orders from the group's operations in Indonesia, China, Vietnam and Singapore.
Profitability was hit by start-up costs of a Malaysian subsidiary and larger minority interests, company officials said.
